name: FINLAND

flag.title: Finnish Flag
flag.note: White field with blue Nordic cross

lead: Finland is at the top of Europe. Green northern lights blaze on winter nights. In summer the sun barely sets. Finland has about 188,000 lakes and forests full of elk. Finns invented the sauna.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Finland is so flat that standing on a hill is exciting. About 75% of the land is trees, mostly pine and spruce. In winter, everything turns white. The north dips below −30 °C.
Lapland lies north of the Arctic Circle. In midwinter the sun does not rise for weeks. In summer the midnight sun never sets.
animals: About 2,000 brown bears live in Finland's forests, near the Russian border. The brown bear is the national animal. Ancient Finns saw it as a great forest spirit.
The whooper swan is Finland's national bird. It nests on quiet lakes. Elk are so common that road signs warn drivers.
culture: Finns value quiet, honesty and sisu. Sisu means gut-grit, the strength to keep going when things get hard. Finland has about three million saunas for 5.6 million people.
Finland gave the world Angry Birds and the Linux operating system. Folk music on the kantele harp tells stories from the Kalevala, an epic poem.
history: Sweden ruled Finland for about 600 years. In 1809 Russia took over. Finland became a Grand Duchy (a semi-independent region). The Kalevala epic came out in 1835.
Finland declared independence on 6 December 1917. In 1940 the Soviet Union invaded. Finland fought hard in the Winter War against a much larger army. It joined NATO in April 2023.
wows: The UN has ranked Finland the world's happiest country eight years running.
With 188,000 lakes, you are never far from water in Finland.
Finnish is one of the few European languages with no Latin, Greek or Germanic roots.
In 1906 Finnish women became the first in the world to vote and run for parliament.
The sauna tradition is thought to be thousands of years old.
Santa Claus's official home is Rovaniemi, right on the Arctic Circle.
Sámi herders move about 200,000 reindeer across Lapland on routes mapped over centuries.

myths.fact: Strictly, Scandinavia means Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Finland is a Nordic country.
Polar bears live on Arctic sea ice, far from Finland. No wild ones live there.
